args:
In the context of my career project, I need to prepare for my Virgin Australia interview. I've put the full PD in my onedrive inbox. I also asked Jaimyn who referred me what to expect, here is what Jaimyn said Heya! Yeah she mentioned, and she also gave you great feedback too. Harry (my other colleague who started when I did) and our engineering lead who recently started will run the round 1 interview. If you get to round 2 it should be run by our head of AI/myself (not sure if I still would with the potential perceived conflict from referring you but I assume it’s fine).

In terms of the round 1 interview, it’s pretty high level. There’s no coding challenges or leet code exercises etc. so don’t stress about preparing for that. We have a list of questions we go through and expect you to answer in your own words (a little ironically, using AI at all is an instant fail haha).

These range from a few very specific pointed questions to test the depth of knowledge across AI systems and frontend JavaScript/react and python/APIs to some more high level stuff to see how you approach problem solving. Things that would be useful to brush up on are your AI system fundamentals (RAG, safety systems, evals etc) and react hooks/python API fundamentals. We definitely don’t expect you to get everything “right” or go into too much detail, but it’s definitely helpful of course.

I was considering this, but I feel like giving you the question list may be unfair but given your experiences I think you’ll be fine. ;). I need to work out prep. There are a few things I want to do: 1. Brush up on anything mentioned in the PD or the job ad, that I have previously given you. 2. Particulaly brush up on Fast API fundametals. I haven't used it before but I want to show I understand it. 3. Things I should know as a senior level python dev. 4. The key things Jaimyn mentioned. 5. How I would design the enhancements I have proposed for LIMSOC as a staff level AI engineer. (I can give you a futher brief on these, but I essentially want to consider these problems now so I can use them as examples in the interviews).
